Methods for Sampling and Test for Petroleum and Related Products of Natural or Synthetic Origin (excluding

FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 143) (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft 
finalized by the Methods for Sampling and Test for Petroleum and Related Products of Natural or Synthetic Origin 
(excluding Bitumen and Hydrogen) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related 
Products Division Council. 


This Indian Standard describes a procedure for examination and evaluation of white mineral oils. The ultraviolet 
absorption of white mineral oils is used to determine the suitability of white mineral for applications like food, 
drug, and cosmetic. 


This standard was first published in 1993 and was based on ASTM D 2269-88. This first revision ofthe standard 
has been taken up to align it with the latest version of the standard ASTM D2269-10 ‘Standard test method for 
evaluation of white mineral oils by ultraviolet absorption’. 


In the formulation of this standard, assistance has also been derived from ASTM D2008-12 ‘Standard test method 
for ultraviolet absorbance and absorptivity of petroleum products”. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in Annex B. 


In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or 
calculated, is to be rounded off, it shallbe done in accordance with IS 2 : 2022 *Rules forrounding offnumerical values 
(second revision)’. 


IS 1448 (Part 143) : 2022 


Indian Standard 


METHODS OF TEST FOR PETROLEUM AND ITS PRODUCTS 


PART 143 EVALUATION OF WHITE MINERAL OILS BY 
ULTRAVIOLET ABSORPTION SPECTROSCOPY 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This test method standard describes aprocedure 
for the examination and evaluation of white mineral 
oils. 


1.2 This test method is not applicable to oils 
containing additives soluble in dimethyl sulphoxide 
(DMSO) that show fluorescence or fluorescence 
quenching properties. 


1.3 This standard does not purport to address all of 
the safety-problems associated with its use. It is the 
responsibility of the user of this specification to 
establish appropriate safety and health practices and 
determine the applicability of regulatory limitations 
prior to use. 


2 TERMINOLOGY 


2.1 Transmittance, T 


Radiant power transmitted by the mineral oil extract 
in its cell divided by the radiant power transmitted 
by the solvent controlin its cell. 


2.2 Absorbance, A 
The logarithmto the base 10 of the transmittance, 7 
multiplied by -1: 

A= —log,)T 


2.3 Sample Path Length 


The distance between specimen surface on which 
the radiant energy is incident and the specimen 
surface from which it is emergent, in cm. 


2.4 Concentration, c 


The quantity of the sample dissolved in a unit 
quantity of solution, in g/l. 


2.5 Absorptivity, a 


The absorbance divided by the product of path 
length and concentration, as given below: 


A 


~ bc 


3 OUTLINE OF THE TEST METHOD 


A sample of oil is extracted with dimethyl 
sulphoxide and the ultraviolet absorbance of the 
extract is determined in the range from 260 nm to 
350 nm. Under similar condition, the absorbance is 
measured for naphthalene standard and the 
absorbance is compared with the sample. 


4 APPARATUS 


4.1 UV-Visible Spectrometer 


Should be equipped to handle liquid samples in 1 cm 
path length cells. The Spectrometer shall be capable 
of measuring absorbance with a repeatability of 
+ 1.0 percent or better from an average at the 0.4 
absorbance level in the spectral region at around 290 
nm with a band width of 1 nm or less. 


4.2 Fused Quartz Cells 


Two, having path lengths of 1.00 cm + 0.005 cm, or 
better. 


4.3 Separatory Funnels, Glass Stoppered 


125 ml capacity, equipped with PTFE stop-cocks or 
other suitable stopcocks that will not contaminate 
the solvents used. 


5 REAGENTS AND MATERIALS 


5.1 Solvents 
5.1.1 Normal Hexane 


Hexane (AR grade), having an ultraviolet light 
absorbance not exceeding 0.02 nm down to 260 nm 
when measured in a 1 cmcell. The purity shall be 
such that the solvent control as defined in 6.3 shall 
have an absorbance curve compared to water 
showing no extraneous impurity peaks and no 
absorbance exceeding that of dimethyl sulphoxide 
compared to water at any wavelength in the range 
260 nm to 350 nm, inclusive. 


Warning — Extremely flammable, harmful if 
inhaled (see A-1). 


5.1.2 Iso-octane (UV Spectroscopy Grade) — For 
use as a Spectroscopic solvent. 


IS 1448 (Part 143) : 2022 


Warning — Extremely flammable, harmful if 
inhaled (see A-2). 


5.1.3 Dimethyl Sulphoxide 


For use as spectroscopic solvent. Pure grade with 
99.9 percent dimethyl sulphoxide, clear, water 
white, melting point 18.5 °C, with an absorbance 
curve compared to water not exceeding 1.0 nm at 
264 nm and showing no extraneous impurity peaks 
in the wavelength range up to 350 nm when 
measured through a path length of 1 cm. 


Warning — Combustible, rapidly absorbed through 
skin (see A-3). 


5.2 Naphthalene — More than 99 percent purity. 


5.3 Standard Reference Solution 


A solution containing 7.0 mg ofnaphthalene per litre 
of purified iso-octane. 


5.4 Standard Reference Spectrogram 


The absorbance curve obtained by scanning the 
standard reference solution in the range from 260 
nmto 350nm against iso-octane ofthe same spectral 
purity as that used to prepare the standard. 


5.5 Standard Reference Absorbance 


The absorbance at 275 nmof the standard reference 
spectrum. 


NOTE — This absorbance will be approximately 0.30. 
6 PROCEDURE 


6.1 In a separatory funnel, transfer 25 ml of the 
mineral oil, then add 25 ml of hexane into it and mix 
thoroughly. Add 5.0 ml of dimethyl sulphoxide into 
the funnel and vigorously shake the mixture for at 
least 1 min. Allow the mixture to settle and wait for 
the lower layer to be clear. 


6.2 Take another separatory funnel and transfer the 
lower layer to it, add 2 ml of hexane and vigorously 
shake the mixture. Allow the mixture to settle and 
wait for the lower layer to be clear. Collect the lower 
layer, designated as mineral oil extract, into a 1 cm 
cell. 


6.3 Take another separatory funnel, add 5.0 ml of 
dimethyl sulphoxide and 25 ml of hexane. Shake 
vigorously for at least 1 min and allow the mixture 
to settle until the lower layer is clear. Collect this 
lower layer, designated as solvent control, into a 
1 cm cell. 


6.4 Determine the absorbance of the mineral oil 
extract and compare to the solvent control in the 
range 260 nm to 350 nm inclusive. 


7 CORRECTION FOR INHIBITOR CONTENT 


7.1 If sufficient amount of the inhibitor is present in 
the sample, a correction for the absorbance due to 
same inhibitor may be made as described below. The 
inhibited sample should be available to prepare a 
blend and the concentration of additional inhibitor to 
be added to the inhibited sample should be equal to 
the concentration contained in the inhibited sample. 

NOTE — Usually, the inhibitor content is expressed in 

pounds per thousand barrels. Pound per thousand barrelsx 


0.002 85 = grams per litre. For example, 5 Ib/1 000 barrels 
x 0.002 85 = 0.014 25 g/litre. 


7.2 Weigh about 50 mg of inhibitor in a volumetric 
flask, fill to volume with inhibited sample and 
thoroughly mix it. Further dilute with inhibited 
sample, if required, to obtain the desired 
concentration of added inhibitor. 


7.3 Measure absorbance of the original inhibited 
sample and label it MEAS-A. 


7.4 Measure absorbance of the blend containing 
known amount of added inhibitor and label it 
MEAS-B. 


7.5 Calculate the difference in absorbance between 
MEAS-B and MEAS-A at corresponding spectral 
positions, as follows: 


AA= A, — A; 


where 


AA difference in absorbance at a given 

spectral position; 

Aa = absorbance of MEAS-A at the same 
spectral position; and 

Ab = absorbance of MEAS-B at the same 


spectral position. 


7.5.1 Correct the absorbance at each spectral 
position as follows: 


A, = Ay — AA 
where 
Ac = corrected absorbance at each spectral 


position. 


7.6 Mark the points of inflection on the spectrogram 
from MEAS-A at wavelengths lower and higher 
than those which were increased. 


7.6.1 Draw a baseline tangent to the curve 
connecting the two points. 


7.6.2 Read the absorbance Ag, along the baseline at 
each spectral position. 


7.7 Compare Aa and A. at each position, if A. is less 
than Ag, it is indicated that the inhibitor content of 
the original sample is less than the amount added. 


7.8 Use the absorbance A. or Aa, whichever is 
greater, to compare to the solvent control in the 
range 260 nm to 350 nm, inclusive. 


8 REPORT 
Report the difference between the absorbance ofthe 


mineral oil extract and the solvent control at the 
wavelength desired. 


9 PRECISION AND BIAS 
9.1 The precision of this test method as obtained by 


statistical examination of inter laboratory test results 
is as follows: 


9.1.1 Repeatability 


The difference between consecutive test results 
obtained by the same operator with the same 


IS 1448 (Part 143) : 2022 


apparatus under same operating conditions on 
identical test material, in the normal and correct 
operation of the test method, exceed 0.014 
absorbance units only in one case in twenty. 


9.1.2 Reproducibility 


The difference between two single and independent 
results obtained by different operators working in 
different laboratories on identical test material, 
under same operating condition of the test method, 
exceed 0.044 absorbance units only in one case in 
twenty. 


9.1.3 These precision data were obtained on 
absorbances in the wavelength region 275 nm to 
280 nm. 


9.2 Bias 


This procedure has no bias because the value ofthe 
absorbance can be defined only in terms of a test 
method. 


IS 1448 (Part 143) : 2022
